entries.title: Fourier subset entropy bound for unit-norm real functions (Li-Han)
entries.statement: Let f:{-1,1}^n -> R have E[f^2]=1 under the uniform product measure. Let p(S)=hat f(S)^2, I_i=sum_{S containing i}p(S), I=sum_i I_i, and H_e=sum_S p(S) ln(1/p(S)), with zero terms interpreted continuously. Then H_e <= I + sum_i I_i ln(1/I_i). This bound does not require f to be Boolean-valued.
entries.proof_text: Parseval makes p a probability law on subsets. If S has law p, the entropy subadditivity inequality for its n coordinate membership bits gives H_e(S)<=sum_i h_e(I_i). For 0<=u<=1, h_e(u)=u ln(1/u)+(1-u)ln(1/(1-u))<=u ln(1/u)+u. Summing proves the claim, including endpoints by continuity.

source.excerpt: for all real-valued Boolean functions of unit L2-norm

entries.title: Failed bridge: absorb Han's coordinate correction into total influence
entries.statement: The proposed universal inequality sum_i I_i(f) log_2(1/I_i(f)) <= C I(f) for every Boolean f and an absolute constant C is false. Therefore the Li-Han extra-term entropy bound does not imply the Fourier Entropy-Influence conjecture by absorbing its coordinate correction; further Boolean-specific information is required. This is a refuted route, not a counterexample to FEI.

entries.title: Conjunction witnesses unbounded Han correction to influence ratio
entries.statement: For n>=2 let f_n:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} be +1 only when all inputs are +1, and -1 otherwise. Each coordinate influence is 2^{1-n}; hence I(f_n)=n 2^{1-n} and sum_i I_i(f_n) log_2(1/I_i(f_n))=(n-1) I(f_n). The ratio grows without bound. This refutes only the correction-absorption bridge; it is not a counterexample to FEI.

relations.rationale: Witness card says the ratio is n-1; bridge card says one absolute C would bound that ratio for every Boolean f.
Bridge card concerns absorbing sum_i I_i log(1/I_i); theorem card retains exactly that correction in its upper bound.
Bridge card says the absorption route fails; existing P0162 card asks for H(f)<=C I(f) for every Boolean f.
